ai.title: CLI wrapper prints crash diagnostics for SIGILL and SIGSEGV
ai.summary: The CLI release wrapper adds `printCrashDiagnostics` to detect and report `SIGILL`, `SIGSEGV`, `SIGBUS`, and `SIGABRT` exits, including Windows NTSTATUS equivalents like `0xC000001D`. It also introduces `resetTerminal` to emit ANSI escape sequences clearing alternate screen, mouse, and bracketed paste modes when the child process is killed. This applies to `cli/release/index.js` and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`, ensuring the parent process cleans up terminal state and provides actionable error messages for binary compatibility issues.

eli5.text: When the assistant's command-line tool crashes in a way that usually leaves your terminal messed up (like frozen screens, broken cursor, or weird paste behavior), the tool now automatically fixes your terminal and prints a plain-English message explaining what likely went wrong, such as your computer's processor not being new enough to run it. You would notice the difference as a readable error message instead of a silent crash, and your terminal would no longer require manual resetting after such a failure. This behavior is live today in the released command-line versions, and it was added alongside the version 1.0.638 release.

ai.title: Remove evalbuff and expensivebuff
ai.summary: Deleted evalbuff directory and references in AGENTS.md. Removes documentation and code for the eval optimization loop. Scope limited to repo structure and agent docs.

eli5.text: The project removed a large set of files (about 9,300 lines across 57 files) that supported an experimental workflow for automatically improving documentation by running coding assistants against past commits and analyzing the results. That workflow, along with its guides and specs, is no longer part of the repository. Anyone reading the internal docs will no longer see references to it, but this does not change how the coding assistant itself behaves day to day.

ai.title: CLI fix agent cancellation lock release
ai.summary: Immediate release of chain lock and queue state on user abort in `send-message.ts`. Previous behavior held lock until `client.run()` resolved, blocking new messages. New logic updates `isProcessingQueueRef` and `setCanProcessQueue` directly in abort handler. `handleRunCompletion` and `use-send-message.ts` skip redundant state resets if `abortController.signal.aborted` is true.

eli5.text: When you press Esc to stop an in-progress assistant message, the program now frees up the queue immediately so you can send your next message right away instead of waiting or getting stuck. Previously, the program held onto a lock until the full background task finished, which could block new messages. The fix moves the cleanup into the moment you cancel, and skips redundant resets afterward so a newer message run isn't disturbed.

ai.title: Expand top-freebuff-users script with detailed metrics
ai.summary: The `top-freebuff-users.ts` script now accepts a configurable `agentId` argument (default `base2-free`) and expands output to include detailed per-user statistics such as daily/hourly activity, token usage, and cache hit rates. It aggregates data via additional SQL queries for daily and hourly distributions, rendering ASCII bar charts for time-of-day and day-of-week usage patterns. Default lookback window increased to 168 hours (1 week) and limit reduced to 50 users. Internal tooling only; no user-facing changes.

eli5.text: The internal admin tool that tracks which free assistant users are most active now shows a much richer profile for each person, including how many messages they send per hour and per day, their token usage, and how often they benefit from cached responses. The time window it looks back at grew from 3 days to 1 week, and the default list now shows the top 50 users instead of 200, making the detailed report easier to read at a glance. You need the configurable agent ID argument (defaulting to 'base2-free') to point it at the right assistant version, and it renders ASCII bar charts so you can spot when users prefer to chat, all for internal tooling only, with no changes visible to end users.

ai.title: Change Stop button label to Esc
ai.summary: Stop button label updated from Stop to Esc in cli/src/components/stop-button.tsx. Reflects keybinding convention for interrupting execution. Affects CLI surface only.

eli5.text: When you see a stop button in the command-line tool, you now see the word Esc instead of Stop, matching the keyboard shortcut that cancels the current action. You just notice the label change on that button; the button still does the same thing when clicked.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 1.0.638
ai.summary: Version bumped 1.0.637 to 1.0.638 in cli/release/package.json. This is a release-bump commit with no functional changes, packaging the user-visible CLI, model picker, and cancellation fixes shipped since the previous release.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in `cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `1.0.637` to `1.0.638`; analysis notes describe this as a release-bump with no functional code changes.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.638 makes the tool more stable, keeps your terminal clean when things go wrong, and improves how agents learn from documentation before doing work. When the program crashes unexpectedly (like from incompatible software), it now shows a clear diagnostic message instead of a confusing freeze, and it automatically resets your terminal so leftover display states don't mess up your screen. A new April Fools package called expensivebuff was briefly added then promptly removed, leaving the actual changes focused on reliability. The background system now releases locks immediately when you cancel a task, so you can start a new message right away instead of waiting. Upgrading gives you faster, cleaner cancellations and much clearer error feedback if something breaks, plus a more organized documentation setup that helps the AI agents understand your project rules better. The 'Stop' button is now labeled 'Esc', matching keyboard conventions so it's intuitive to interrupt whatever is happening.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI release bumped to 0.0.28
ai.summary: The CLI release package manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was updated from version 0.0.27 to 0.0.28, bundling user-visible improvements from the same-day commit sequence. This release captures the preceding work including the CLI wrapper crash diagnostics for SIGILL/SIGSEGV signals, the agent cancellation lock release fix in `send-message.ts`, the Stop button label change to Esc in `cli/src/components/stop-button.tsx`, and the notable top-freebuff-users script metrics expansion. The version bump is the sole content of this commit, with all functional changes having landed in earlier commits within the 2026-04-02 release sequence.
ai.evidence: Modified file `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` shows a single-line version change from `"version": "0.0.27"` to `"version": "0.0.28"` in the CLI release package manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.28 brings better crash handling, smoother agent cancellations, and cleaner documentation. When the CLI crashes unexpectedly, it now prints clear error messages and resets the terminal properly so your screen isn't left in a broken state. If you abort a running agent, it releases locks immediately, letting you send new messages without waiting. The documentation was reorganized, with obsolete planning files removed and the authentication guide renamed for clarity. An April Fools' joke package called expensivebuff was briefly added and then removed, leaving only the real Freebuff and Codebuff packages. Upgrading gives you a more reliable terminal experience, especially during crashes or interruptions, along with tidier docs.
